What is the length of $a$ in the triangle shown above?
question.worked_solution:
Here, we know the lengths of the hypotenuse and one leg, so let $b=\frac{15}{2}$ and $c=\frac{39}{2}.$ We need to find $a,$ the length of the other leg.

According to the Pythagorean theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}^{2} & ={a}^{2}+{b}^{2} \\ {a}^{2} & ={c}^{2}-{b}^{2} \\ a & =\sqrt{{c}^{2}-{b}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in the values for $b$ and $c$ gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\sqrt{{(\frac{39}{2})}^{2}-{(\frac{15}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1\,521}{4}-\frac{225}{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{324} \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$
